title: उत्तरपर्व · अध्याय १८३

items.text:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि दानमन्यत्तवोत्तमम् ॥
महाभूतघटं नाम महापातकनाशनम् ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
|| śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca || ||
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dānamanyattavottamam ||
mahābhūtaghaṭaṃ nāma mahāpātakanāśanam || 1 ||

items.text:
पुण्यां तिथिं समासाद्य स्वनुलिप्ते गृहांगणे ॥
कारयेत्कांचनं कुंभं महारत्नान्वितं पुनः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
puṇyāṃ tithiṃ samāsādya svanulipte gṛhāṃgaṇe ||
kārayetkāṃcanaṃ kuṃbhaṃ mahāratnānvitaṃ punaḥ || 2 ||

items.text:
लोकपाला महेन्द्राश्च स्ववाहनसमास्थिताः ॥
ऋग्वेदः साक्षसूत्रश्च यजुर्वेदः सपंकजः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
lokapālā mahendrāśca svavāhanasamāsthitāḥ ||
ṛgvedaḥ sākṣasūtraśca yajurvedaḥ sapaṃkajaḥ || 5 ||

items.text:
वीणाधारी सामवेदो ह्यथर्वा स्रक्छुभान्वितः ॥
पुराणवेदो वरदः साक्षसूत्रकमंडलुः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
vīṇādhārī sāmavedo hyatharvā srakchubhānvitaḥ ||
purāṇavedo varadaḥ sākṣasūtrakamaṃḍaluḥ || 6 ||

items.text:
सप्तधान्यानि पुरतः स्थापयेच्छक्तितो बुधः ॥
पादुकोपानहच्छत्रं चामराग्र्यासनायुधान् ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
saptadhānyāni purataḥ sthāpayecchaktito budhaḥ ||
pādukopānahacchatraṃ cāmarāgryāsanāyudhān || 7 ||

items.text:
एवं प्रकल्प्य विधिवन्महाभूतघटं नरः ॥
गुडसारोपरिगतं माल्यवस्त्रैरथार्चयेत् ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ prakalpya vidhivanmahābhūtaghaṭaṃ naraḥ ||
guḍasāroparigataṃ mālyavastrairathārcayet || 8 ||

items.text:
अथ पर्वसमीपे तु स्नात्वा नियतमानसः ॥
त्रिः प्रदक्षिणमावृत्य मंत्रमेतमुदीरयेत् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
atha parvasamīpe tu snātvā niyatamānasaḥ ||
triḥ pradakṣiṇamāvṛtya maṃtrametamudīrayet || 9 ||

items.text:
यस्मान्न किंचिदप्यस्ति महाभूतैर्विना कृतम् ॥
महाभूतमयश्चायं तस्माच्छांतिं ददातु मे ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
yasmānna kiṃcidapyasti mahābhūtairvinā kṛtam ||
mahābhūtamayaścāyaṃ tasmācchāṃtiṃ dadātu me || 10 ||

items.text:
अत्र सन्निहिता देवाः स्थापिता विश्वकर्मणा ॥
ते मे शांतिं प्रयच्छंतु भक्तिभावेन पूजिताः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
atra sannihitā devāḥ sthāpitā viśvakarmaṇā ||
te me śāṃtiṃ prayacchaṃtu bhaktibhāvena pūjitāḥ || 11 ||

items.text:
इत्येवं पूजयित्वा तु महाभूतघटं नरः ॥
ब्राह्मणं पूजयित्वा तु भूषणाच्छादनादिभिः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
ityevaṃ pūjayitvā tu mahābhūtaghaṭaṃ naraḥ ||
brāhmaṇaṃ pūjayitvā tu bhūṣaṇācchādanādibhiḥ || 12 ||

items.text:
महाभूतघटं दद्यात्पर्वकाले यतव्रतः ॥
पुनः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य ब्राह्मणं तं क्षमापयेत् ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
mahābhūtaghaṭaṃ dadyātparvakāle yatavrataḥ ||
punaḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya brāhmaṇaṃ taṃ kṣamāpayet || 13 ||

items.text:
अनेन विधिना यश्च दानमेतत्प्रयच्छति ॥
एकविंशत्कुलोपेतः शिवलोके प्रयात्यसौ ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
anena vidhinā yaśca dānametatprayacchati ||
ekaviṃśatkulopetaḥ śivaloke prayātyasau || 14 ||

items.text:
पुण्यक्षयादिहाभ्येत्य राजा भवति धार्मिकः ॥
अजेयः शत्रुसंघातैर्महाबल पराक्रमः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
puṇyakṣayādihābhyetya rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ ||
ajeyaḥ śatrusaṃghātairmahābala parākramaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
अष्टापदोत्तमघटं विमलं विधाय ब्रह्मेशकेशवयुतं सहलोकपालैः ॥
क्षीराज्यपूर्णविवरं प्रणिपत्य भक्त्या विप्राय देहि तव दानशतैः किमन्यैः ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
aṣṭāpadottamaghaṭaṃ vimalaṃ vidhāya brahmeśakeśavayutaṃ sahalokapālaiḥ ||
kṣīrājyapūrṇavivaraṃ praṇipatya bhaktyā viprāya dehi tava dānaśataiḥ kimanyaiḥ || 17 ||

items.h: इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे महाभूतघटदान विधिवर्णनं नाम त्र्यशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ।। १८३ ।।

en_summary: Krishna gives the gift of the jar of the great elements (mahabhuta-ghata), which destroys even the great sins. On a holy day, in a well-plastered courtyard, a gold jar with great jewels is made, from a span to a hundred finger-widths across and from five to a hundred palas of gold, filled with milk and ghee and topped with a wish-granting tree. In it are Brahma, Vishnu and Maheshvara on lotus seats, the world guardians and Indra on their mounts, and the Vedas in their forms: the Rigveda with a rosary, the Yajurveda with a lotus, the Samaveda with a vina, the Atharvaveda with a fine garland, and the Purana-veda giving boons, with rosary and water pot. The seven grains, sandals, shoes, an umbrella, a whisk, a fine seat and weapons are set before it, and it is placed on a heap of jaggery and worshipped with garlands and cloth. At the festival the bathed, self-controlled patron walks around it three times and prays: "Since nothing at all exists without the great elements, and this jar is made of them, may it give me peace; may the gods set here by Vishvakarma, worshipped with devotion, give me peace." He honours the Brahmin with ornaments and clothes, gives him the jar at the festival time, walks around again and asks his pardon. The giver goes to Shiva's world with twenty-one generations, and when his merit is spent returns as a just king, unconquerable by hosts of enemies, mighty, devoted to the warrior's duty, learned and a worshipper of gods and Brahmins. Make a spotless gold jar with Brahma, Shiva, Keshava and the world guardians, filled with milk and ghee, bow to it and give it to a Brahmin; what need of a hundred other gifts?
